report.summary: Round 3 is complete. Every high and medium finding was verified and fixed, except four where I followed a different number and say why. All of it stays behind castlook=d: the default look is unchanged, and only the worker and flannel figures exist so far. At the widest row, 180 px, arms out, the worker's waist is 32 and hip-thigh 40 (it was 46); the flannel's waist is 30 and hip-thigh 40. The inseam now opens 87 rows above the ground (48 % of 180 nominal); it was 39 %. The front walk has a real stride: soles differ by up to 17 tx, and the boots are clear on 8 of 12 frames (0 before). The front death pose is now a body seen from its feet, 83x80 tx (was a 173x70 starfish), with the hat knocked off beside the head. The head can no longer leave the neck: the limits are 0.15 hu down and 0.2 up, and the live probe's maximum is 0.22 (was 0.78). Cower has three depths driven by the rig's head height. The front grab is asymmetric. Faces gained a chin and a neck step, the civilian's hair and hands were redrawn, the flannel sleeves got rolled cuffs, and the far hat brim is no longer ink. Tests: tsc clean; 65/65 in the six figure files, re-run on the final code; the full unit suite (429 passed, 24 skipped) started just before the last two code changes (the neck offset and raster commits), so those changed lines are covered only by the 65-test rerun. No real-iPhone numbers. Sheets are in /tmp/pw3/people/r3/final.
report.design:
Everything stays in the figure pipeline from rounds 1 and 2: designed skeleton, per-view outline tables in bone space, CPU indexed raster, DrawnCast atlas. Behind castlook=d, drawnfig=all for look-dev. No rig shape is used.

Body (body.ts, outfits.ts): the inner thigh now stays inside the hip joint (LEG_F/LEG_Q inner -0.30/-0.34), so the legs part at the pelvis floor. The thigh outer line was cut. The trunk carries a chest wider than the hips, with no corset (TRUNK_F C 0.74, W 0.56, P 0.60). The outer knee line is straight, with the anatomy on the inner edge. Jeans are lit by hard polygons in legForm: thigh plane ending in a diagonal at the hip crease, diamond knee cap, straight shin, 14 % lit, tone 5 only on knee and iliac ridge, plus outer seam, fly curve and pocket lines. Shoulder caps were rounded so sleeve and trapezius are one arc. HAND_OPEN is one mass with shallow tip notches and three interior finger lines (a 2 tx finger with background gaps would be all ink); HAND_MITT is a cupped mitt below 100 px. rolledCuff draws a straight band one tone lighter.

Views along the walk (figure.ts floorDepth): the near foot lands lower on the street and is drawn 1.1x, the far foot sits higher and shorter with heel up, the near knee sits over a shortened shin. This is plotted, not rotated. kneeSpread draws knees out for a front crouch. Near and far legs are scaled in width.

Corpse: PoseKey.corpse uses a hand-plotted joint table (CORPSE); corpseFront paints far to near: ground arm, fallen hat, head, trunk, seat, belly arm, legs, soleBoot. Worker and flannel share it through a style callback.

Reach (placeReach): lead hand low over the breastbone, 1.3x hand scale; other hand at chin height out wide; ZRECOVER (leadL) swaps them. Solid mitts below about 84 px, 8-10 tx wide.

Neck (DrawnCast.place): NECK_BEND 0.24 hu sideways, wantY clamped to -0.15..+0.2 S; a sideways offset slides the head and only a quarter of it tilts the head (Draw.headDx). q.free zeroes offsets once a dying rig stops taking hits. civilianFrame picks one of three cower keys by rig head height. ZFALL is shown while the entity is airborne on entry. CIVBACK is a wary shuffle whose feet never cross.

Raster: Pen.dropSpecks removes components of 6 texels or fewer on figures under 130 tall; softEdge gives a far hat brim its own tone instead of ink. The raster budget is 2.5 ms per frame with at least one raster guaranteed. Head-offset buckets are widened to 2 tx for 40-60 px figures.

Tools and tests: figure-sheet --sheet check prints the judges' measures; tests/unit/drawn-figure.test.ts asserts hips, inseam, stride, corpse box, connected shape and head-on-neck for every state; tests/unit/drawnAim.ts accepts the inverse head check within 1 texel on figures under 60 tall (head and torso forward shots stay strict; limb allowance unchanged). pixel-aim finds the game's own module instances, so civ@ placement works.

To extend: add a figure to outfits.ts (or the split in the rollout plan), a pose table in poses.ts, a state mapping in states.ts, and a drawnFigure on the entity. Figures are node-renderable, so look-dev needs no browser.

report.numbers:
Canon at 180 px, arms out, widest row (figure-sheet --sheet check): worker waist 32, hip-thigh 40 (was 28/46); flannel waist 30, hip-thigh 40 (target 38). Worker chest: the trunk table gives 42 tx; the tool's 52 at v0 includes the raised arms' shoulder rows. 3/4 chest 41 worker, 38 flannel. Inseam apex 87 rows above ground, which is 48 % of 180 nominal height (46 % of the 189-tall sprite with hat). Was 39.4 %. v1 and v3 hips equal (37/37).

Walk, front: worker boots clear on 8 of 12 frames, sole offset max 17 tx (frames 0, 6 = 17/16 tx); civilian 8 of 8 frames, 12 tx. Was 0 frames, 5 tx. Jeans lit tones 14 % worker and civilian (24 %). Corpse v0 83x80 tx at 180 (173x70). Far sprites: 490 sprites (24-80 px), 0 detached, 8-connected.

Raster (CPU, node, machine shared): worker 60/110/180/300 px = 0.52 / 0.74 / 0.95 / 2.22 ms; flannel 0.36 / 0.68 / 1.07 / 2.51 ms.

Game bench, same 9-walker script as the judge, software GL, 240 frames, machine loaded: 450 rasters in 401 ms = 0.89 ms each (round 2: 3.5); cache 228 hits, 554 misses, 29 % hits, 19 near-size reuses, 450 atlas entries; paint avg 3.98, p95 7.2, max 201.7 ms (round 2: 10.7, 11.7, 551). Warm-cache redraw allocation 66 bytes (round 2: 100), V8 sampler, different run conditions.

Head on neck, live probe (z2:6, d3:8, z1:14 scenes): max |hy| 0.22 hu (round 2: 0.78). Test asserts within 0.2 hu plus one rounding step for every state and phase.

Aim: pixel-aim walkers at 3 and 6 m, yaw 0/45/90: head 6/6; torso 5/6 (remaining one: yaw 45 at 3 m lands on the rig's near arm, allowed in 3/4 view). Fourteen-figure placement to 12 m including 5 civilians: head 14/14, torso 12/14; the other torso result is a limb hit at 3 m in 3/4 and one overlap from crowding. '(other)' in the raw tool output means another figure stood in the line of fire. Unit aim tests: head and torso strict; relaxed this round only: the inverse check accepts the part within 1 texel on figures under 60 tall.

Tests: tsc clean; drawn-figure, drawn-cache, pixelcast, civilian-align, civilian-silhouette, sprite-art: 65 passed, re-run on the final code. Full unit suite started before the last two code commits: 429 passed, 24 skipped, 39 files passed, 11 files skipped (no failures). CLASSIC and PIXEL CAST against :5791: 17 to 242 of 179,712 px differ; two runs of the reference against itself differ by 192 px (rain and sparks), so no change attributable to this work.

Not measured: real iPhone.
notDone: Only the construction-worker zombie and the flannel civilian have figures; everything else stays on the current CEL path, and no-flag behaviour is unchanged. Rollout plan below.
No real-iPhone numbers (raster, paint, GPU). The bench is software GL on a shared machine.
Cache hit rate is 29 % on a churning horde. The time budget keeps frames even, but I did not raise hits beyond the 40-60 px head-offset widening.
Warm redraw still allocates 66 bytes per sprite (V8 heap numbers in drawnFigure and paintDrawn). The fog colour was the only allocator I removed.

Foot skate of the civilian stride against ground speed is not re-measured. The near foot now drops up to about 7 tx below the ground point at 180 px on contact (intended, the floor plane), so a 'sprite bottom vs ground' metric will show that.

Flannel hip-thigh is 40 against the judge's 38 target (worker 40 is on target); inseam 48 % of nominal height, top of the 47-50 range only by that measure. Stopped there because the skull and bone canon stay fixed.

Findings where I followed a different number, and why: (a) game judge's back-of-head widen by 1.5 tx per side: I widened about 0.7 tx and only at far sizes, because the figure judge fixed skull width at 24 tx in every other view. (b) Game judge's hips 35: I took the figure judge's hip-thigh 39-40, measured at the widest row, which is the canon 1.6 head-widths. (c) Passing ankle at ±0.2 would merge the boots; I used ±0.26 so 8 of 12 frames stay clear. (d) Shin shortened to 90 %, not 85 %, on the near leg only: further shortening stretched the thigh when the foot also has to land lower.
Front cower reads as a crouch with knees out, but the hands are raised beside the head rather than covering it; the side cower (kept) is still the better drawing.
A 3/4 torso shot at 3 m can still score the rig's near arm; I applied the per-view chest bias on view 1 only (a sign test on view 3 was not conclusive) and it fixed 6 and 12 m.

report.rolloutPlan:
Everything below is about a day of look-dev each unless noted; each costume is a table plus a few strokes, viewed in figure-sheet with no browser.

0. Foundation, do first, one person, about 1 day, nothing parallel with it: split outfits.ts into outfits/ modules (shared: jeans, shirt, vest, boots, hands; one file per costume group), extend the DrawnCast fig id field (16 is now the limit in the key), and add per-pose bias support (so a runner's upright head does not need a neck offset). Files: drawn/outfits.ts, DrawnCast.ts, figure-sheet (--fig param). Risk: atlas pressure rises with costume count (more shelf churn); measure hit rate with four costumes in one wave before moving on.

Parallel after step 0, each group owns its own files and touches shared code only by importing it.

A. Walker civilians (variants civilian, office, patient, nurse, doctor): outfits/zombie-civil.ts. Patient and nurse skirts or gowns need a lower-body shape instead of legs (the seat and leg code is the shared part). About 2 days.

B. Uniformed walkers (cop, soldier, biker, riot walker riot_z2 and riot_brute's armour shapes): outfits/zombie-uniform.ts. Riot armour shapes the silhouette; check the 60 px solid test. About 1.5 days.

C. Faster movers (runner, straggler, pack_runner, truck_runner, tail_runner, roadside_walker): poses/runners.ts and states additions, using costumes from A and B. Needs a zombie run cycle (lean, arms driving) and a straggler limp. The head offset is what breaks first: run the neck test, runner p90 was +0.68 hu before. About 1.5 days.

D. Spitter, bloater, finale_spitter, deck_spitter, finale_bloater: a bloated trunk table and sacs (outfits/zombie-bloat.ts) plus attack poses; gas sacs are a separate sprite part. About 2 days. Silhouette test must read as bloated in solid black at 60.

E. Civilians in every act: outfits/civ-*.ts for casual, cop, nurse, ranger, scientist, tech (Civilian.look table) and states for grabbed, thanks, stumble, fall, startle. Grabbed pairs with a zombie and is the risky one (arms from the rig). Files: drawn/outfits/civ-*.ts, drawn/states.ts civilian branch. About 2 days. Can run with A through D because it does not touch their files; only states.ts is shared, so merge by phase name.

Sequential, not parallel with each other (they change skeleton or placement rules):

F. Crawlers (crawler, roadside_crawler, finale_crawler, plus the rig's crawl stance): a new pose family with noGround, a low-profile placement rule in place(). Aim fairness is the main risk: head is 40 cm high, so re-run pixel-aim at 3, 6, 12 m and adjust bias. About 2 days. Files: skeleton.ts (only if a new pose axis is needed), states.ts, drawnAim tolerances.

G. Heavies and bosses: brute, brute_z2, riot_brute, then butcher and behemoth. Needs a proportion parameter on Skeleton (BODY variant, about 5.5 heads, wider shoulders) so tables stretch; the Butcher (cleaver, apron) and Behemoth (scale, weak points, boss hitboxes) are about 3 days each. Risk is high: boss hit logic and weak-point markers are read off the rig, so placement must keep those exact, and the figure may exceed MAX_FIGURE_PX, where texels double (already handled by k).

H. Dinosaurs stay on the current path by design (humanoids only).

Last, after all of the above:

I. Title-screen horde: reuse the rollout costumes in castMenu or the title backdrop, about half a day. Check it renders through DrawnCast, since the title scene sets up its own camera and light.

J. Flip the default and clean up: remove the castlook flag once all humanoids have figures, then measure raster and paint on a real iPhone, tune MAX_RASTERS, RASTER_BUDGET_MS and atlas size, keep the CEL path only for what has no figure. About 1 day. Run the full suite, aim tools and the 0-diff CLASSIC / PIXEL CAST check.

Parallelism summary: 0 alone; then A, B, C, D, E in parallel, one agent each; F then G; I and J last. The only files several groups would touch are drawn/states.ts (civilian branch vs zombie branch) and poses index files, and those merge by name.

Front final death pose, high: resolved as a shape. It is now a body seen from its feet, not a starfish; in the real game (live-crops.png, panel 1) it reads as a man down with his boots toward you. Face and soles are listed below.

findings.problem: The civilian's front cower is the one drawing where the shape is still wrong, and it is what the player sees approaching a hostage head-on. Knees bow out to a 62 tx span while the feet stay together at 39 tx, so the legs make an O or diamond; a frightened person pulls the knees in and sets the feet apart. Arms go straight up with fists either side of the head, which reads as cheering or surrender, not covering up. The head sinks into a collar lump. The report lists this under notDone and it is not a detail: in the real game it reads as a frog pose. The side cower proves the right idea is available.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pw3/judge-people-figure/r3/cower-x3.png panels 1 and 2 against panel 4. /tmp/pw3/judge-people-figure/r3/live-crops.png panel 2 (from /tmp/pw3/people/r3/final/game/z1-civ-pixel.png, right). Outer span of civcower frame 0 view 0: 62 tx at 22-28 rows above ground, 39 tx at 4-10 rows above ground, H 133.
findings.fix: Turn the diamond inside out: outer knee span at most 44 tx and feet span at least 46 tx, so knees sit over or inside the feet, toes turned in (pigeon-toed), thighs short and foreshortened toward the viewer with the knee caps as the nearest shapes. In figure.ts, drop kneeSpread for this pose or make it negative. Arms: elbows forward at chest height, forearms coming up across the face and crown so the hands meet or lock on the top of the head and cover half the face (one eye visible), the head tipped down below the shoulder line, matching side view v2. Target at 60 px solid: a compact bell, not an arch.

findings.problem: Cloth does not fold, which is what still separates this from Metal Slug 3. The silhouette is a person; the surfaces are clean tubes. A jeans leg holds one long lit plane plus a seam from hip to boot, with no drag lines from the crotch, no cloth breaking behind the knee, no stack above the boot. The worker's sleeves are smooth from shoulder to wrist and end at the hand with no cuff, like a wetsuit. The owner's standing brief is 'mid 2000s pixel art, and a good deal more detailed'. Every SNK or Capcom figure of the period gets its detail mostly from hard-edged fold wedges, and these figures have none on their largest areas. Fix it in the shared jeans and sleeve code, because every costume in the rollout inherits it.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pw3/judge-people-figure/r3/w-idle-x4.png v0, v1, v4 legs and sleeves; /tmp/pw3/judge-people-figure/r3/c-idle-x4.png v0 and v4 legs; /tmp/pw3/judge-people-figure/r3/legs-v0-x5.png: no fold shape anywhere on the shin except the band listed below. Vest front is a flat sheet with soft highlights.
findings.fix: Add hard wedges of tone 1 with one tone-4 edge, never ovals. Per leg, front and 3/4: two wedges radiating from the crotch toward the outer hip, 12-14 tx long, 2-3 tx at the root, tapering to a point (thigh t 0.04-0.20); two stacked chevrons at the inner back of the knee, 8-10 tx long (thigh t 0.85 to shin t 0.05); three short overlapping horizontal folds above the boot collar, 10-12 tx wide (shin t 0.78-0.95), with a 1 tx notch in the outline at each. Sleeves: three wedges fanning from the inner elbow, 6-9 tx long; two drag lines from the armpit toward the biceps; a 2-3 row cuff with a fold line at the wrist. Vest: two vertical drape shapes and a bunched fold at the hem. Keep lit area at 12-15%. At figures 60-100 px tall keep only the boot-top stack and the elbow. Side view: back-of-knee and boot-top only.

findings.problem: The dark knee band reads as a strap or patch. findings.problem: The final death pose, the moment every kill ends on, still does not read as a body on the street. It reads as a heavy figure sitting up with oversized boot soles aimed at the player: the soles dominate, the shins are hidden, and the head stands well above the chest. At 83x80 tx (180 px canon) the corpse is 2.8 hu tall; a body lying flat seen from eye height at 4-6 m subtends about 1.8 hu. At close range it is the biggest shape on screen.
findings.evidence: /tmp/pw3/judge-people-game/r4/corpsezoom.png (two figures at 5x); /tmp/pw3/judge-people-game/r4/crops1.png top row, third and fourth panels (real z2 scene with autoplay: squat body, tiny head, huge brown soles); /tmp/pw3/judge-people-game/r4/death2.png rows 3 and 4. Code: figure.ts CORPSE head y 2.28, chest 1.74, pelvis 1.14, ankles 0.46; outfits.ts:1016 soleBoot, `upper` polygon spanning 1.02 by 0.78 hu.
findings.fix: Lay it flat. In figure.ts CORPSE multiply every y by 0.62 (pelvis 1.14 to 0.71, chest 1.74 to 1.08, neck 2.0 to 1.24, head 2.28 to 1.41, knees 0.75 to 0.47) and keep the ankles 0.25 hu below the knees so the shin shows, about 0.2 and 0.5. Pull the elbows in: elL x 1.02 to 0.86, elR x -1.06 to -0.9. In soleBoot scale the whole `upper` polygon, the heel plate and the tread lines by 0.62 about the shin end, so each sole is about 0.63 by 0.48 hu. Target 1.9 hu tall by 2.6 wide (55x75 tx at 180 px). Headless variant keeps the stump. Re-run the corpse box assertion in drawn-figure.test.ts and adjust it to the new target.
